{
  "entityC1": {
    "design_critique": "1) The sensing-geometry lever is not isolated. Iteration 3 changed sensor y, sensor spread, wheel_track (0.12 to 0.14), kp, ki, kd and base_speed together, so its gain over iteration 2 cannot be credited to sensing alone. This draft again changes sensor y (0.06 to 0.08), sensor count (5 to 7), spacing (0.015 to 0.01), kp (2.0 to 1.6) and ki (0.1 to 0.05), and the rationale attributes the result to the sensing change. If the score moves, the team will not know which change caused it.

2) The line-loss pattern is unexplained. Every trial in iterations 0, 2 and 3 shows exactly one line-loss event and then an off-track end, on every track and seed. Since gains had no effect in iterations 0 and 2, the single loss is probably a fixed start or early-curve event, and the off-track end follows because last_direction at throttle 0.35 does not recover the line. The draft does not state this recovery failure, and it does not test the line_loss rule, which is the variable most directly tied to the observed pattern.

3) The speed choice conflicts with the completion goal. base_speed stays at 1.2, and the course needs roughly 1.5 m/s average to finish in 3 s. The draft gives no estimate of the speed that 1.2 produces, and no evidence that a finish is reachable at this setting. Progress was 0.15 at best in iteration 3. Without completion, the score is at most about 250 times progress plus the line-loss and rms terms, so progress gains alone can add only modestly. The draft should say whether it is optimising survival (progress) or completion, and what speed it needs.

4) kd = 0.3 is untested and likely to kick the wheels. kd acts on the per-second change in signal. With 7 sensors at 0.01 m spacing the signal changes more smoothly than before, which helps, but a change of 0.3 per 10 ms step is 30 per second, times kd 0.3 gives about 9 turn units, roughly 3150 PWM. That is close to saturation at every tape transition. No race has yet isolated kd, so keeping it at 0.3 for damping is an assumption, not a result.

5) The reduction in kp is not supported by the evidence it cites. The rationale says the gain sweep showed no benefit from high gain. Iterations 0 and 2 showed no effect from gains at all, which is different from showing that low gain is better. Reducing kp to 1.6 may weaken the correction on the slalom and tight bends, where the line leaves the sensor array quickly.

6) The sensor-count argument is wrong in its stated mechanism. The rationale says the fewer-sensor signal is already scaled up by the wider weights. The weights are a linear mapping of position, slope about 50 per metre. Iteration 3 used the same slope (weight -1.5 at x=-0.03, -0.75 at x=-0.015). The new 7-sensor weights therefore give essentially the same signal-to-offset mapping. The change is finer sampling, not a rescaled signal, so the claim about scaling should be removed.

7) The outer sensors at x=plus or minus 0.03 m see the tape only when the line centre lies within about 0.03 + 0.008 + 0.0125 m of the sensor. This is not checked for the sharpest bend, and the first line loss may still occur there.

8) The footprint of 0.016 m on 0.01 m spacing means each tape position covers about four to five sensors at once. The signal is then a smoothed centroid, which reduces sensitivity to small offsets near the centre. The trade-off is not discussed.

9) Mass, body and yaw inertia (about 0.0027 kg m squared) are not discussed, and the draft does not say whether the turn response is limited by the body or by the sensing.",
